note: Four proxy-grade items that net slightly positive: a record storage end-market for the fastest-growing segment and a 10-Q note removing the self-insurance left tail, against an airline-cost drag on 13% of revenue.

The first guide has to show a gross margin without the 904bp one-time refund and a decelerating top line, with the greenshoe stabilising bid gone; the halved interest bill after the debt paydown is the real offset.

Five quarters of backlog burn against flat revenue and the 10-K's 90%-shipped statement put Q1 FY27 revenue well below the year-ago comp on a no-analyst, 2k-share-a-day name; the VWR/Dodge booking proxies are the only thing cutting the other way.

Guidance is the line this stock pays on and two record commercial deals signed after the last guide plus a Champions League year land in the first FY27 guide, with 8% of a small float short; the Q4 revenue shortfall sits inside the company's own range.

The 8% Section 338 sell-off hit goods already under Section 232 and mostly Mexico-origin, and tomorrow's call is the venue where that gets said; the IEEPA refund read-across from Polaris is a smaller one-off, and the flat MY27 price sheet was already guided.

An audited negative-equity balance sheet, a falling SOL-per-share KPI and two uncovered Nasdaq deficiencies against a 27%-of-float short, a lender that just eased terms and a SOL rally since year end; the negatives are shrunk for the squeeze.

The 46% slide is the withdrawal of the CEO's 10b5-1 bid rather than priced disappointment, so there is no discount to relieve, and the unexplained Q1 cash outflow against a shareholders' deficit makes the Q2 cash line the swing item.

A +76% run built on a rolled-over buyback that executed 1% last time, while the Q1 revenue was 62% deferred-revenue drawdown and the auditor was swapped for a censured firm; the two hunters' duplicate readings are merged and the tiny non-insider float is the only cushion.

Famous Footwear's -5.9% comp over the identical window leaves a -2.4% consensus stale on a more athletic-exposed banner with no refund cushion, partly offset by the same peers describing a materially better August for the Q3 update.

Kohl's and Dillard's were sold on refund-driven beats and Macy's refund path is less certain, plus a credit-card line consensus models at +8.6% against a guided deceleration; sized small against a strongly calls-bid skew and a name that barely moves on prints.

IAA's +11% units with stated share gains over two of the three reported months implies Copart's insurance units fell faster than last quarter, into a 10% run-up and a name that has fallen after six of seven prints; the CCC deal is a small, wide-banded negative.
